 Esmeri SK1N10, a biodegradable micropowder for skincare and sunscreen products
 By The editorial staff 
 October 22, 2026 
 Share Linkedin Facebook X 
 Esmeri SK1N10 (INCI: Cellulose Acetate Butyrate (and) Disodium Succinate) provides an immediate soft-focus effect, fast drying, and shine control, resulting in a powdery matte finish for aqueous formulations and oil-in-water . The material is described as non-nano in accordance with Recommendation EC 2022/C 229/01 and meets the biodegradability criteria set forth in Regulation (EU) 2023/2055.
 Impact on SPF Formulations
 The micropowder harnesses UV-scattering properties to improve film uniformity and optical performance, creating an SPF-boosting effect that can help reduce the concentrations of UV filters. Esmeri SK1N10 is cited as being compatible with both organic and inorganic filters and suitable for use in creams, sprays, and other sunscreen formulations.
 The ingredient is stated to be compatible with retinoids, hyaluronic acid, and salicylic acid, and can be used in serums, creams, eye care products, and moisturizers. Eastman indicates that performance depends on the overall formulation and must be validated through formulation testing.
 Eastman backs up its claims with an internal survey: 85 % of the formulators surveyed consider sustainability to be essential, and 52 % say they are dissatisfied with current offerings. The Esmeri line is thus expanding beyond color cosmetics into sun care and skin care applications.
